{"id":"PKIX-gphz","title":"pkix-path: signature algorithm coverage (RSA-PSS, P-384, Ed25519, P-521, RSA-SHA384/512)","description":"## Why

Currently `pkix-path::DefaultVerifier` supports only two algorithms:
* RSA-PKCS1v15 + SHA-256 (`1.2.840.113549.1.1.11`)
* ECDSA P-256 + SHA-256 (`1.2.840.10045.4.3.2`)

Real-world chains routinely use other algorithms. PKITS doesn't exercise this much because it's RFC-conformance focused, but a TLS chain in 2026 typically uses one of:

* **RSA-PSS** (`1.2.840.113549.1.1.10`) — preferred in TLS 1.3, used by many modern CAs
* **ECDSA P-384** (`1.2.840.10045.4.3.3`) — common in modern TLS, code signing, sigstore
* **Ed25519** (`1.3.101.112`) — modern TLS, increasingly common

Without these, downstream consumers hitting these algorithms see `AlgorithmNotAllowed` (or worse, the OID dispatcher in `DefaultVerifier` returns `signature::Error::new()` with no useful info). The differential test harness will surface this loudly as `StricterThanWild` once we add a corpus that includes modern chains.

## What

Five new `SignatureVerifier` impl unit-structs in `pkix-path/src/lib.rs`, one per algorithm, each behind its own feature flag. `DefaultVerifier` (`lib.rs:3047`) gains OID dispatch entries for each. Each algorithm reuses the existing RustCrypto crate already in the dependency graph or pulls in a sibling crate (`p384`, `p521`, `ed25519-dalek` etc).

Pattern is established by the existing `EcdsaP256Verifier` (`lib.rs:1867`) and `RsaPkcs1v15Sha256Verifier` (`lib.rs:1909`) — copy and adapt per algorithm.

## Recommended decomposition (file children when work starts)

1. **RSA-PSS-SHA256 verifier** (P2) — most-impactful single algorithm. Note: PSS has algorithm parameters (saltLength, mgf1HashAlgorithm) that must be parsed from `AlgorithmIdentifier`. There are multiple 'valid' PSS encodings in the wild — this is itself a divergence class the harness should surface.
2. **ECDSA P-384 + SHA-384 verifier** (P2) — `p384` crate exists in RustCrypto.
3. **Ed25519 verifier** (P2) — `ed25519-dalek` or `ed25519` crate.
4. **RSA-PKCS1v15 SHA-384 + SHA-512** (P3) — extends existing RSA verifier with two more OIDs.
5. **ECDSA P-521 + SHA-512** (P3) — `p521` crate.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Each algorithm has its own `SignatureVerifier` impl, feature flag, and unit tests using independent oracles (RustCrypto test vectors, RFC 4231/8032 test vectors, NIST CAVS).
- [ ] `DefaultVerifier` dispatches to all enabled verifiers via OID match.
- [ ] No new test uses `pkix-path` itself as the oracle — every test verifies against a known-correct independently-computed signature.
- [ ] `pkix-difftest run pkits ...` baseline unchanged (PKITS doesn't exercise these algos, so all chains stay in their current buckets).
- [ ] A new sample chain (real-world cert with one of these algos) added to `pkix-difftest/tests/fixtures/` and exercised by the existing smoke tests.
- [ ] No `unsafe`. No new top-level workspace deps that pull in C/C++.
- [ ] `pkix-path` stays `no_std` — every new verifier opt-in via feature flag and the underlying crate is no_std-capable.

## Out of scope

- ML-DSA / Dilithium (covered by `pkix-composite` follow-up).
- DSA (deprecated; not implementing).
- ECDSA over non-NIST curves (secp256k1, brainpool).
- RSA-PSS-SHA384, RSA-PSS-SHA512 (file as a follow-up if needed; PSS-SHA256 covers the bulk of real-world use).

## Filed as

{"notes":"Superseded in substance by PKIX-dzjn (2026-11-25): the algorithms this describes are implemented.

pkix-path/src/verifiers.rs dispatches RSA-PSS (OID_RSASSA_PSS, verifiers.rs:74), Ed25519 (OID_ED25519, :90) and ECDSA P-521 (OID_SECP521R1, :59, dispatched :213), and the rustcrypto umbrella feature is rsa + p256 + p384 + p521 + ed25519.

What is actually left is a different thing, and it is tracked in PKIX-dzjn: pkix-path default = ["rsa", "p256"], so a default build gets RSA and P-256 only. Per the project decision of this date, everything in RustCrypto should be available everywhere, which means changing the defaults rather than implementing anything.

Not closing these unilaterally since they are not mine to triage wholesale, but they should not be worked as written."}

STALE -- the algorithms this describes are implemented, and the real remaining work (the defaults) is now done too. Closed under PKIX-dzjn.

Evidence, verified rather than assumed: pkix-path/src/verifiers.rs dispatches RSA-PSS (OID_RSASSA_PSS, verifiers.rs:74, used at :304/:399/:505), Ed25519 (OID_ED25519, :90, used at :537) and ECDSA P-521 (OID_SECP521R1, :59, dispatched :213). The rustcrypto umbrella feature is rsa + p256 + p384 + p521 + ed25519.

What was genuinely missing was not implementation but DEFAULTS: pkix-path had default = ["rsa", "p256"], so a caller who did nothing got a verifier that rejected a P-384 chain as unsupported_key -- correct behaviour, baffling default. Fixed in 758ce9f1: default = ["rustcrypto"], shipped as pkix-path 0.4.2.

That change had a consequence worth recording here, because it is the kind of thing a future reader of these beads will hit. ed25519 pulls ed25519-dalek, hence curve25519-dalek, whose build script selects an x86 SIMD backend that fails on x86_64-unknown-none with "rustc-LLVM ERROR: Do not know how to split the result of this operator!" -- the same error the bare-metal CI job already worked around for sha2. Fixed in 2a33baf5 by extending that flag list rather than weakening the gate; thumbv7em and riscv64 were unaffected. pkix-path Cargo.toml documents the flags for consumers building that target.

The regulated-environment half is also done and tested (dd45bada): an algorithm a build will not perform surfaces as SignatureNotVerified { reason: UnsupportedAlgorithm }, distinct from SignatureInvalid, all the way out through pkix_chain::Error. Four tests in pkix-chain/tests/regulated_algorithms.rs cover UnsupportedAlgorithm, UnsupportedKey, MalformedKey and the negative case.

PKIX-qws.4 (legacy SHA-1 verifiers) is deliberately NOT closed by this and must not be actioned: SHA-1 is refused by design.

{"notes":"CORRECTION 2026-11-25, same day: the SHA-1 aside in this bead closure was wrong.

It said PKIX-qws.4 "must not be actioned" because "SHA-1 is refused by design". That was my inference from DefaultVerifier having no SHA-1 backend, not a decision anyone made, and it contradicts the repository own docs -- PKIX README:227 reads "legacy SHA-1 (feature-gated, off by default, for validating old chains)" and :311 lists it as a P1.

Confirmed stance: VERIFY-ONLY, OPT-IN, OFF BY DEFAULT. PKIX-qws.4 is real work and remains open. Nothing signs with SHA-1 and nothing should, so there is no "create" side; the opt-in feature should sit outside the `rustcrypto` umbrella so that umbrella stays "algorithms we recommend".

Everything else in this closure stands -- RSA-PSS, Ed25519 and P-521 are implemented and the defaults are fixed. Only the SHA-1 sentence was false."}
